title: Where does the shift come from?

study.title: Where does the shift come from?
study.summary: Separate an injected location term from differential temperature and common clock drift.

inputs.label: Selected mode
inputs.meaning: An assumed identified mechanical mode, not a frequency derived from this illustration.

inputs.label: Temperature mismatch
inputs.meaning: Test-sphere temperature at B minus A after reference correction; K is kelvin.

inputs.label: Mode temperature coefficient
inputs.meaning: Assumed calibration slope; ppm means parts per million. Must be measured for the actual mode.

inputs.label: Injected location term
inputs.meaning: Synthetic test signal only, with zero as the established-model null.

inputs.label: Common clock drift
inputs.meaning: Same fractional drift applied to test and reference channels; cancels in their ratio.

assumptions: First-order small fractional shifts; matched common clock factors cancel exactly in the defined ratio.
The reference has no differential temperature change in this toy model. No measured sphere coefficient or mode identification is supplied.
The paired 3D specimens have illustrative 0.16 m centre spacing; they are not LOC-1 positions A/B, which are 0.40 m apart. Test/reference object roles and position labels must be assigned separately.
setup: Start with the preserved Copper Sphere Lab and its source-bound model contract.
For a proposed physical study, identify a mode, acquire both test and stationary reference channels on a shared timebase, then calibrate temperature and mounting response.
Freeze randomized blinded A/B positions, sham moves, orientation swaps, exclusion rules and an uncertainty budget before collection.
controls: Set injected location term to zero and vary temperature.
Change common clock drift: the ratio result must stay constant.
Swap sensors and mounts, include sham motion and hold-out temperature calibration.
study.falsifier: An alleged location signal that follows differential temperature, mounting, readout gain or clock mismatch does not discriminate the location hypothesis.
study.scope: Synthetic differential-ratio teaching model. The OSF registration pd3st was independently retrieved. This toy uses B/A relative change in ppm; LOC-1 specifies 10^9*(mean r_A - mean r_B) in ppb (parts per billion), with covariance and equivalence analysis. These estimands differ in sign, normalization and unit. This is not a replication or registered analysis.

metrics.label: Apparent ratio shift
metrics.meaning: First-order differential thermal term plus deliberately injected location term.

metrics.label: Frequency equivalent
metrics.meaning: Selected assumed mode times the fractional ratio shift.

metrics.label: Thermal contribution
metrics.meaning: Can imitate the location signal unless independently calibrated.

warnings: No uncertainty interval or detection claim is inferred from this deterministic example.
The illustrated sphere dimensions do not determine the selected 250 kHz mode.

equations.meaning: r is a dimensionless ratio, D is its A/B fractional change in parts per million. Common multiplicative drift cancels.
First-order teaching approximation. alpha is an assumed calibration slope in ppm/K that must be measured for the actual mode; dT is differential kelvin; epsilon is a synthetic location term in ppm.

glossary.Pa: Pascal, pressure equal to one newton per square metre.
glossary.K: Kelvin, the SI unit of temperature; temperature differences of 1K and 1°C have equal size.
glossary.ppm: Parts per million; a relative value multiplied by one million.
glossary.ppb: Parts per billion; a relative value multiplied by one billion.
glossary.RLC: A circuit containing resistance R in ohms, inductance L in henry and capacitance C in farad.
glossary.RMS: Root mean square, a waveform amplitude convention distinct from peak.
glossary.DAC: Digital-to-analog converter, the electronic stage that turns numeric samples into a voltage.
glossary.EEG: Electroencephalography, a measured scalp electrical signal; not simulated here.
glossary.SPL: Sound pressure level, an acoustic measurement requiring calibration.
glossary.GLB: Binary glTF, a 3D scene file format; this file contains illustrative geometry.
glossary.SVG: Scalable Vector Graphics, a vector drawing format.
glossary.OSF: Open Science Framework, the repository hosting the independently retrieved registration.
glossary.TOST: Two one-sided tests, an equivalence-testing method; its margin and uncertainty need a declared plan.
glossary.A: Position or condition A in the named protocol; not an ampere unless explicitly stated.
glossary.B: Position or condition B in the named protocol; not magnetic flux density unless explicitly stated.
glossary.LOC1: The external Sphere location-comparison protocol, with its own registered estimand.
